title: Flip Div Game
statement:
Andy is playing the Flip Div Game.

He is given two integers:
- N – the initial number.
- K – the divisor.

Initially, N is guaranteed not to be divisible by K.

Andy must flip exactly one bit in the 32-bit binary representation of N. Flipping a bit means:
- 0 -> 1
- 1 -> 0

After flipping exactly one bit, determine the smallest bit position (1-based from the right) such that the resulting number is divisible by K.

If no single-bit flip makes the number divisible by K, return -1.

### Bit Numbering
Treat N as a 32-bit integer:
- The rightmost bit is at position 1.
- The next bit to the left is position 2.
- ...
- The leftmost bit is at position 32.

Input Format:
- input1: An integer N.
- input2: An integer K.

Output Format:
- Print a single integer representing the minimum bit position that should be flipped so that the resulting number becomes divisible by K. If no such bit exists, return -1.

examples.explanation:
Binary representation of 3: 00...0011.
Flipping bit 1 -> 2 (not div by 5)
Flipping bit 2 -> 1 (not div by 5)
Flipping bit 3 -> 7 (not div by 5)
Flipping bit 4 -> 11 (not div by 5)
Flipping bit 5 -> 19 (not div by 5)
Flipping bit 6 -> 35 (35 % 5 == 0 -> YES!)
Minimum bit position = 6.
Flipping any one of the 32 bits of 3 never produces a number divisible by 10. Return -1.

constraints: N is initially not divisible by K.
hints: Iterate bit position i from 1 to 32.
Flip bit i using bitwise XOR: flipped = N ^ (1LL << (i - 1)).
Check if flipped >= 0 and flipped % K == 0.
Return the first bit position i that satisfies the condition, or -1 if none found.
discussion: Bitwise XOR and modulo checking across 32 bit positions in O(32) = O(1) time.
